findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil, so `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and the request 500s instead of unsubscribing.
findings.failure_mode: Unhandled NoMethodError during request handling produces a 500 error.
findings.impact: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil, so `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and the request 500s instead of unsubscribing.
findings.root_cause: New code assumes `TopicUser.find_by(...)` always returns a record and calls methods on the result without a presence check.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard for a nil `tu` (create/return early or use TopicUser.change) before reading/writing `notification_level`.
findings.title: unsubscribe dereferences possibly-nil TopicUser
findings.trigger: A logged-in user opens the unsubscribe URL for a topic for which no TopicUser row exists (e.g. they never viewed/tracked it, or the row was deleted).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R105 shows `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` which returns nil when no record exists. Line R107 immediately calls `tu.notification_level` without nil check, causing NoMethodError. Trigger is realistic: user clicks unsubscribe link for topic they never viewed.

The claim about 'all add_unsubscribe_link callers' breaking is speculative without proof of callers not supplying the argument.
